clue.text: Sounds like the Fraud Squad's brief game played in court

indicators.note: the clue says the phrase it describes is only similar when spoken, so the spoken form stands for the spelt one

parts.note: the job of a police fraud squad is to crush swindles, i.e. to squash rackets

explanation.surface: A tennis-style match staged before a judge, with detectives somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: A racket is a fraudulent scheme, so the Fraud Squad's brief (remit) is to squash rackets, said the same as the court game's name. The Fraud Squad is the British police unit for financial crime.
explanation.definitionFit: This indoor racket sport is played in a walled court, a sense of 'court' the surface hides behind law courts.

clue.text: Fleet takes southern and treacherous part of beach

parts.note: fleet as an adjective means swift

explanation.surface: A navy squadron lands on a dangerous shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterlogged sand that swallows anything heavy is a hazard found on some shores.

clue.text: Almost everyone sits on the German tree

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece is placed above, sitting on, the second
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: everyone means all
der is the German masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Nearly the whole crowd perches on a German tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a common waterside tree of the birch family.

clue.text: Hunters do the weeding it's traditionally lucky

parts.note: a hunter is a horse bred for riding to hounds
to hoe is to clear weeds with a garden tool

explanation.surface: Fox-hunting folk turn their hand to gardening, a lucky habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunters' suggests people, but here they are horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved iron shoe nailed above a door is an old good-luck charm.

clue.text: A lord is the inventor of signaller's lamp

parts.note: Ld is the abbreviation for Lord in titles

explanation.surface: A peer turns out to have devised the signalling lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Aldis devised the handheld signal lamp used to flash Morse code between ships.

clue.text: Insect breeders surrounded by swarms of workers and bossy women

definitions.text: Insect breeders surrounded by swarms of workers

explanation.surface: Domineering women, like hive rulers, ringed by busy staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The egg-laying ruler of a hive lives amid worker swarms, and the same name is used for imperious, domineering women.

clue.text: Take off top of radiator-it doesn't need cooking

indicators.note: take off the top of means drop the first letter of the word

parts.note: a radiator is a heater

explanation.surface: Remove the cover of a radiator and you have something raw.
explanation.walkthrough: Eating apples are called eaters in Britain, as against cookers, which need cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit sweet enough to eat raw is known as an eater, as opposed to a cooking variety.

clue.text: Big meals need mushrooms

explanation.surface: Banquets call for fungi.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish laid-out feasts are spreads, and to mushroom is to expand rapidly, which is what something that spreads does.

clue.text: Palm on desert island yields nut

indicators.note: the run of letters sits inside the words like an island and they yield it up

explanation.surface: A palm tree on a desert island bears nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The almond is the edible kernel of a fruit tree, sold as a nut.

clue.text: Landowner set out to catch rustlers' leader

indicators.note: one piece catches, i.e. encloses, the other

parts.note: to lay out a table is to set it out, so laid means set out

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A landowner lays a trap for the chief cattle thief.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landowner.
explanation.definitionFit: Laird is the Scots title for the owner of a landed estate.

clue.text: Dog embarrassed crossword compiler

parts.note: embarrassment makes someone go red
the person who writes a crossword is its setter

explanation.surface: A dog shames the puzzle-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish setter, with its chestnut coat, is a gundog breed.

clue.text: It will produce acorns to rake off before the end of June

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second in the answer
off in the sense of gone bad or wrong marks letters to be rearranged
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: rake up the acorns before the end of June.
explanation.definitionFit: Acorns are the nuts of the oak, so this plant yields them.

clue.text: Crooned tune backwards, drunk in Spain

parts.note: to croon is to sing softly, so crooned is sang

indicators.note: backwards tells you to read this word right to left

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A tipsy singer in Spain performs a song in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' is not about the singer: it means swallowed, the drink's own sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish wine punch with fruit.

clue.text: Bird doctor comes across a kite without it

indicators.note: the doctor meets the second piece, placed next to it
without means these letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A vet chances upon a kite that is missing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without it' removes IT from AKITE, leaving AKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A drake is a male duck.

clue.text: A beefsteak dish between courses, including cream of tomato starters

indicators.note: the first piece includes, or holds, the second

parts.note: an entree was originally a dish served between the main courses

indicators.note: the starters of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A menu listing steak, entree and cream of tomato soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrecote is a French cut of steak from between the ribs.

clue.text: Nocturnal insectivores are evasive, greedy creatures

parts.note: to hedge is to avoid giving a straight answer
hogs are pigs, proverbially greedy

explanation.surface: Night-time bug-eaters are shifty and gluttonous animals.
explanation.definitionFit: These spiny small mammals forage at night for beetles and worms.

clue.text: Get rid of Heather's puddings

parts.note: to dump something is to get rid of it
ling is another name for heather, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Throw out the puddings Heather made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name; it is the plant, also called ling.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumplings are balls of dough, and in British usage pudding can mean any such stodgy dish.

clue.text: Rye do best production and The Pearl Fishers could open down there

definitions.text: The Pearl Fishers could open down there

indicators.note: a production, as of an opera, puts letters into a new form

explanation.surface: Rye stages a show of Bizet's opera The Pearl Fishers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pearl Fishers is an opera by Bizet, so 'open' and 'production' read as theatre; Rye is an English town.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers looking for pearls would open molluscs on the seabed bank where they grow.

clue.text: Fog conceals 500 and there's 500 sheets in the middle of the river

definitions.text: in the middle of the river

indicators.note: the first piece conceals the second inside it

parts.note: a mist is a thin fog
D is the Roman numeral for 500
a ream of paper is 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A foggy river where five hundred sheets float about.
explanation.definitionFit: Midstream means the central part of the current, away from both banks.

clue.text: With Monsieur not well mother used to collect water to turn machines

definitions.text: used to collect water to turn machines

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for the French Monsieur
not well means ill
dam is a mother, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: A sick Frenchman's mother once fetched water to drive machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A millpond's barrier stored water so it could drive a waterwheel.

clue.text: Japanese dish in restaurant gives us hiccups

indicators.note: in tells you the answer is sitting inside the following words

explanation.surface: A diner complains that Japanese food at a restaurant gives them hiccups.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is vinegared rice with raw fish, a Japanese staple.

clue.text: Tuck in if still outside school

indicators.note: the first piece goes outside, around, the second

parts.note: inert means motionless, still

explanation.surface: Tuck into food if you are still outside the school gates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuck in' suggests eating; here it means push something in.
explanation.definitionFit: To insert is to put or push something into place.

clue.text: Although deaf, interpret what's said using pre-dial arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement puts these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A deaf person understands speech using a telephone dial setup.
explanation.definitionFit: Deaf people can follow speech by watching mouth movements.

clue.text: Seafood left uncooked in Portugal and Norway

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal
N is the international vehicle code for Norway
left uncooked is raw

explanation.surface: Fish served raw in Portugal and Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: Prawns are shellfish eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Condescend to listen to Scandinavian

indicators.note: to listen to means the word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: a Dane comes from Denmark in Scandinavia

explanation.surface: Lower oneself to hear a Nordic visitor out.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to stoop to doing something thought beneath one.

clue.text: Leo's partner is no less confused having caught one

indicators.note: the mixed letters catch, enclose, the other piece
confused means the letters are mixed up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A zodiac lion's mate is no less muddled after catching something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' turns NOLESS into LONESS, which takes in I.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is the lion, and a female lion is his mate.

clue.text: Old-fashioned party is best

parts.note: something out of style is out
a do is a party

explanation.surface: An old-style party is the finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best' is a verb here, to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to beat or surpass them.

clue.text: Twisting in road can become very severe

indicators.note: twisting means the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A bend in a road can be very dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Draconian means harshly strict, after the Athenian lawmaker Draco.

clue.text: Fleshy stem underground beginning to rot

parts.note: the Tube is London's underground railway

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fleshy root below ground starts to rot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underground' looks like part of the definition, but it is the Tube, London's Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato is a swollen underground stem storing food.

clue.text: Chopped meat with single blades, to put things delicately

parts.note: mince is finely chopped meat
single means one
swords are blades

explanation.surface: A butcher chops meat with single blades.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means to speak tactfully, avoiding blunt language.
